## Narration that sounds like a person, and sharper video

- **Claude Code script writer (optional).** Turn on "Polish the script with Claude Code" to have the Claude Code already signed in on your computer say each line the way a presenter would. Every rewritten line is checked against what the browser actually did: the same quoted control names, no invented numbers or names. A line that fails the check keeps its recorded wording. Nothing is sent unless you turn it on.
- **Chapter titles.** Each page becomes a chapter with a short title ("Pricing Plans", not "the pricing page"). Claude Code writes them when the script writer is on, and chapters survive you editing the line that opens them.
- **Review the script before the voice.** A new Record option stops after the script is written and keeps the video silent. Read and fix any line in the Studio, then press **Add the voice**.
- **Delivery styles.** Warm, calm, upbeat or authoritative, applied to Kokoro (pace and a voice blend), ElevenLabs (expression, and the lines around each one for natural flow) and OpenAI voices (spoken delivery instructions).
- **Your own voice.** With an ElevenLabs key, an uploaded voice sample of your own voice is cloned once and used as the narrator.
- **Pronunciation dictionary.** `WALKCAST_PRONUNCIATIONS="Kunj = koonj; Estate360 = estate three sixty"` fixes a name once, for every recording. It changes what is spoken, never what is shown.
- **Sharper capture.** The page is now captured at 4 to 8 Mbit/s instead of Playwright's roughly 1 to 2, with the same constant 30 fps. If the high-quality capture cannot start the standard video is used, and `WALKCAST_HQ_CAPTURE=0` turns it off.
- **Cleaner audio and video.** The narration track is faded at each clip edge, compressed gently and set to -16 LUFS. The MP4 encodes at CRF 18 with 160 kbit/s AAC.

### Fixes

- Kokoro no longer loses a narration line to a word missing from its dictionary (product names such as "agentic" or "vercel"): the line is retried with the word split or spelled out, then word by word.
- Hostnames, symbols and abbreviations are rewritten to be spoken naturally; captions on screen are unchanged.
